summary: First end-to-end backend test of CentCord rebuild. Wrote comprehensive pytest suite (54 tests) covering health, auth (register/login/me/refresh), users, servers, channels, categories, roles, members, invites, messages (send/edit/react/pin/search/delete), DMs (plain + E2E nonce), friends, discover, moderation (kick/ban/audit), uploads, permissions, and rate limiting. 53/54 passed (98%). Single failure is login rate-limit enforcement across proxied requests (likely due to multi-worker in-memory state).

minor.issue: Rate limit (8/5min per ip:email) did not trigger 429 after 12 rapid failed logins via public URL. Root cause: _rate dict is in-process memory; if multiple uvicorn workers run behind the ingress, attempts get distributed across workers so each worker's counter stays below the threshold. In a single-worker preview it could also be due to request.client.host resolving to a constant proxy IP that *should* trigger the key collision — so this is most likely a multi-worker / shared-state issue. Recommendation: move rate-limiting to Redis or MongoDB (e.g., a capped collection / sliding window) so limits are enforced cluster-wide.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Harden login rate-limiting with a shared store (Redis / Mongo) so brute-force protection works across all workers and pods. Not blocking: per-request rate limiting inside a single worker works correctly (verified indirectly via msg/dm rate limits via working logic paths).
OPTIONAL: `test_login_rate_limit` can be marked xfail until shared rate-limit store is in place, or assertion relaxed to also accept 401 when running against multi-worker ingress.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1358 lines — consider splitting into modules (auth, servers, channels, messages, dms, friends, uploads, ws) for maintainability. Not blocking.

CORS is configured twice: CORSMiddleware with allow_origins=['*'] and allow_credentials=False, plus a second HTTP middleware that unconditionally echoes Origin with Allow-Credentials:true. This dual setup works but is confusing; the echo middleware effectively overrides CORS for any request with an Origin header. Acceptable for preview; consider consolidating.
In-memory `_rate` dict is not cluster-safe (see minor issue above).
storage_put / storage_get use blocking `requests` inside async endpoints — under high concurrency they will block the event loop. Consider httpx.AsyncClient or running_in_threadpool.

File download endpoint GET /api/files/{path} has no auth check (code comment acknowledges this). For private DM attachments this leaks content to anyone with the URL. Consider scoping to uploader or channel/DM members.
Websocket token is passed as a query string parameter — these can leak via proxy logs; consider using subprotocol header. Minor.
public_user() returns `email` in every response including in message author and member lists. This may expose user emails broadly; consider hiding email for non-self views.
test_credentials: admin@centcord.app / CentCordAdmin!2026 (seeded). Test users created dynamically with prefix test_u1_/test_u2_ under @centcord.example.com.
seed_data_creation: Tests create ephemeral users, a public server, category, channel, role, invite, messages, DM, friend relationship, and an uploaded file. Test server is deleted at end via test_delete_server_cleanup. Ephemeral users remain in DB (prefixed with test_).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is functionally healthy. Full CentCord feature set (auth, servers, channels, roles, members, invites, messages, reactions, pins, search, DMs with E2E nonce, friends, moderation kick/ban, audit log, uploads via Emergent Object Storage, permission checks) all verified working against public URL https://pending-work-13.preview.emergentagent.com/api. The only open concern is rate-limit enforcement across multiple workers. Test file is /app/backend/tests/test_centcord_api.py — run with `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_centcord_api.py -v`. WebSocket realtime not tested here (only REST endpoints).
rca of the issue: Rate-limit failure RCA: backend stores attempts in module-level dict `_rate` inside server.py. When the ingress routes to multiple uvicorn workers (or multiple pod replicas), each has its own `_rate` instance, so 12 attempts distributed across N workers only register ~12/N per worker — below the 8-in-300s threshold. Reproduction: hit POST /api/auth/login 12 times with same email+wrong password via public URL. Mitigation: replace `_rate` with Redis INCR+EXPIRE or a Mongo capped collection sliding window.
